paper.citation: Xinkun Nie and Stefan Wager (2021). Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Biometrika 108(2):299–319. DOI 10.1093/biomet/asaa076
paper.title: Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects
paper.source_version: Published typeset article deposited in NSF PAR, 21 PDF pages; issue year 2021; publisher first-online metadata 2020-09-24
paper.source_locator: Section 4.2, PDF p.9 / journal p.307, equation (9) and following smooth effect definition; Figure 2 PDF p.10 / journal p.308, sigma=1 noise setting

mechanism.name: 随机处理与平滑差值 sigmoid 效应
mechanism.title_en: Random assignment and smooth sigmoid-difference effect
generation_equations: Y|X,A~N(b(X)+(A-0.5)*tau(X),sigma**2), sigma=1, selected from Figure 2 noise levels.

sampling.dependence: Independent individuals; Independent Gaussian coordinates within each individual. Outcome errors and treatment randomization use independent local draws.

assumptions: Consistency and no interference across independent individuals.
Treatment independent of outcome error conditional on observed X; source conditional exchangeability.
Positive probability for each treatment at every finite X; no trimming or new clipping.

properties.notes: Three active covariates; smooth nonlinear baseline and treatment-by-covariate effect. This is Section 4.2 equation (9), not the already registered Section 6.1 Setup A. d=10 and sigma=1 come from the source equation and Figure 2, respectively.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full original covariate population; binary treatment 1 versus 0.

truth.expression: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the full original covariate population; binary treatment 1 versus 0.
truth.derivation: X2-X1 is symmetric about zero. expit(t)+expit(-t)=1, hence E[tau(X)]=1/2 and population ATE=0.5.

adaptations: Explicit target adaptation: integrate source conditional effect over the original covariate distribution to obtain population ATE; data-generating equations unchanged.
Rename source treatment D or W to A; observed conditional law unchanged.
Independent Python/NumPy implementation; no source estimator fitting or reported performance tables are reproduced.
